HIGH COURT OF MEGHALAYA
AT SHILLONG
NOTIFICATION
No HCM.11/96/2026/COMP/3535 Dated 15th October, 2026
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE (SOP) FOR OPERATION OF MOBILE eSEWA
KENDRA
1. INTRODUCTION
The eCommittee of the Supreme Court of India, in collaboration with the
National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) and the Department of Justice,
Government of India, rolled out the Mobile eSewa initiative which is designed to
deliver technology-driven, citizen-centric legal services to remote, rural locations
with the objective to ensure every citizen benefits from IT and legal services
regardless of their location or background.
The eCourts Project aims to leverage Information and Communication
Technology to enhance access to justice, improve transparency, facilitate efficient
delivery of citizen-centric judicial services and make court-related information and
services accessible to litigants, advocates and members of the public as a whole. In
furtherance of the objectives of the eCourts Project, the Mobile eSewa Kendra shall
function as a mobile extension of the eSewa Kendra established in the Court
Complexes whose primary goal is to take citizen-centric judicial services directly to
the doorsteps of litigants, rural populations, marginalized communities, and remote
regions where access to judicial infrastructure, internet connectivity or digital
facilities is limited.
For the operationalisation and optimum utilisation of the eSewa Mobile Van,
the High Court of Meghalaya formulates this Standard Operating Procedure.
2. SHORT TITLE, APPLICATION AND COMMENCEMENT
I These Guidelines shall be called the Standard Operating Procedure for Mobile
eSewa Kendra under the eCourts Project.-:
1
11. They shall apply to the High Court, the High Court Legal Services, District
Courts, the Meghalaya State Legal Services Authority, the District Legal
Services Authority, Alternative Dispute Resolution and the mediation
proceedings in pending cases.
They shall come into force from the date of approval by the competent
authority and shall remain in force until modified, superseded or withdrawn.

The principal objectives of the Mobile eSewa Kendra shall be:

Digital Literacy To promote digital literacy in relation to judicial services.
eCourts Awareness: To facilitate awareness regarding various online

The Services of Mobile e-Sewa will be utilised by the High Court of Meghalaya,
Meghalaya State Legal Services Authorities, District Courts, District Legal Services
Authorities (DLSAs), the High Court Legal Services.

5. SCOPE OF THE MOBILE eSEWA KENDRA
The Mobile eSewa Kendra may be deployed in:
• Remote and rural areas;
• Areas having limited access to Court complexes;
• Areas having poor digital infrastructure;
• Geographically difficult areas;
• Villages and administrative blocks located far from District/Sub-Divisional
Courts;
• Locations identified on the basis of demand for judicial services;
• Legal awareness camps, Lok Adalats and other outreach programmes;
• Government/public premises where temporary service camps are organized;
• Other locations as may be approved by the competent authority_
However, this is subjected to a pre-approved deployment schedule.
6. NATURE OF SERVICES
The Mobile eSewa Van shall function as a multi-purpose mobile judicial node.
Services/ activities include, but are not limited to, the following illustrative categories:
6.1 Core eCourts Citizen Services:
a. Information Dissemination: Querying court case status, next date of hearing,
and order/judgment copies.
b. E-Filing Facilitation: Assisting litigants and advocates in e-filing pleadings,
applications, and appeals.
c. Cause Lists & Court Fees: Generation and issuing of e-Courts cause lists and
court fees payment guidance,
d. Certified Copies & Mobile Apps: Providing digital copies of judicial records and
downloading e-Court mobile apps, High Court of Meghalaya Mobile Apps.
e. ePayments: Guiding/facilitating ePayments for different category of matters.
5
6.2 Special Drives & Mobile Adjudication:
a.
b.
C.
d.
MV Act Challan Drives: On-the-spot disposal and digital payment processing
for Motor Vehicle (MV) Act challans etc.
Utility services & Electricity Disputes: Conducting Lok Adalat sessions for
compoundable electricity disputes, water bills, municipal dues and other
matters covered under the scheme
Pre-Litigation Mediation: Pre-litigation mediation camps organized jointly by
MSLSA, DLSA, and TLSAs.
Alternative Dispute Resolution: Court referred mediations, Counselling etc.
6.3 Video Conferencing & Remote Deposition: As per applicable Video Conferencing
Rules.
a.
b

other witnesses via the van's VC setup, as per applicable Video-conferencing
Rules
Stakeholders VC Appearance: Facilitating remote appearance of
litigants/stakeholders in ongoing court proceedings and the Van may be
designated as Court/remote point.
6.4 Legal Awareness & Audio-Visual Campaigns:
a.

NALSA Scheme Outreach: Promoting legal aid schemes, victim compensation
projects, women helpline services, and child rights awareness etc.
7. OPERATIONAL GOVERNANCE & DEPLOYMENT STRUCTURE
7.1 The High Court Computer Committee shall hold overall administrative authority
over van deployment, policy compliance, and inter-agency coordination. It may be
ensured that the optimum utilisation of the Mobile e-Sewa facilities takes place.
6
7.2 MSLSA Nodal Role: The Meghalaya State Legal Services Authority (MSLSA) shall
act as the nodal coordinating agency for scheduling awareness camps, mobile Lok
Adalats, legal aid drives, eServices.
7.3 The High Court Computer Committee shall designate a Nodal Officer for
supervision and coordination of the Mobile e-Sewa facilities,
8. HUMAN RESOURCE & STAFFING ARRANGEMENTS
To ensure smooth service delivery, each Mobile eSewa Van shall be manned
by a dedicated team, comprising of the following.
8.1 Technical Staff: The services of Systems Assistants, eSewa Kendra staff,
eCourts Technical Team members. and other technical personnel from the
establishment of the High Court of Meghalaya or the respective District
Courts may be engaged, as required, to provide technical and IT-related
services such as eCourts Services, e-filing and VC operations during
awareness programmes, special drives, Lok Adalats, and other court-
related outreach activities.
8.2 Legal Aid & DLSA Staff: A Legal Aid Counsel or Panel Lawyer / Para-Legal
Volunteer (PLV) appointed by DLSA or HCLS may handle legal inquiries,
scheme awareness, and grievance intake.
8.3 Driver Engagement: The base vehicle shall be driven by an existing official
driver from the High Court or the Meghalaya State Legal Services Authority.
8.4 . A designated Nodal Officer for supervision and coordination.
9. RECURRING EXPENSES
The recurring expenses for the operations i.e fuel for the VAN & generator, ICT
equipments maintenance, connectivity, operational/incidental cost will be borne by
the High Court of Meghalaya.
10. STATISTICS, REPORTING & FOOTFALL MONITORING
To measure the impact and ensure accountability. the standardized logbook
and reporting mechanism is enforced:
7
10.1 Daily Logbook Entry The Technical Assistant on board shall maintain a
daily logbook recording location visited, distance travelled, total footfall, and
individual service transactions. The Monthly footfall statistics, IT services
availed, and awareness camp numbers shall be transmitted to the Nodal
Officer
10.2 Monthly Reporting: The Monthly footfall statistics, IT services availed, and
awareness camp numbers shall be compiled and transmitted to the
eCommittee & NALSA by the Nodal Officer.
10. REVIEW AND SUPERVISION
10.1 Bi-Annual Performance Review: The High Court Computer Committee
along with the Meghalaya State Legal Services Authority will conduct periodic
bi-annual reviews of services provided through Mobile eSewa Van.
10.2 Modifications & Amendments: Based on feedback from DLSAs and ground
experience, necessary modifications to the SOP may be made from time to
time.

12. INTERNET AND CONNECTIVITY
The Mobile eSewa Kendra should preferably have reliable internet connectivity
through:
• Mobile broadband;
• 4G/56 connectivity
• Multiple network SIMs, wherever feasible;
• Wi-FI hotspot;
• Other approved connectivity solutions.

containing, as appropriate:

The collection of personal information shall be limited to what is necessary for the

14. DAILY CLOSING PROCEDURE
At the end of each working day, the technical staff shall:
1. Ensure that all systems are properly logged out.
2. Shut down computers and other equipment safely.
3. Secure all official documents and equipment.
4. Ensure that no confidential document is left unattended.
5. Verify the inventory of equipment.
6. Record the day's activities.
7. Report any malfunction, loss or incident to the Nodal Officer
8. Ensure safe parking/storage of the Mobile eSewa Kendra vehicle, wherever
applicable.
15. GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL
A mechanism shall be established for receiving complaints or grievances
relating to Mobile eSewa Kendra services.
Complaints may relate to:
• Non-availability of service;
Misconduct;
Delay
Unauthorized charges;

Complaints shall be forwarded to the designated Nodal Officer for appropriate

16. REPORTING AND MONITORING
The Nodal Officer shall submit a periodic report to the competent authority.
1. Number of locations visited;
2. Number of days of operation;
3. Number of users served;
4. Category of services provided;
5. Number of case-status enquiries;
6. Number of orders/judgments accessed/downloaded;
7. Number of persons assisted in accessing eCourts services;
8. Number of awareness activities conducted;
9. Technical issues encountered;
10. Complaints received;
11. Feedback received;
12. Expenditure incurred; and
13. Any other relevant information.
17. COORDINATION WITH LEGAL SERVICES AUTHORITIES
Where appropriate, the Mobile eSewa Kendra may coordinate with the Meghalaya
State Legal Services Authority/District Legal Services Authority for
• Legal awareness programmes;
11
;b
• LokAdalat awareness;
• Awareness regarding ADR mechanisms; and
• Other access-to-justice initiatives.
Such coordination shall not affect the independent functioning of the Judiciary or the
statutory functions of the respective authorities.
18. SPECIAL FOCUS ON VULNERABLE PERSONS
The Mobile eSewa Kendra shall make reasonable efforts to facilitate access for
• Senior citizens;
• Persons with disabilities;
• Women;
• Persons residing in remote areas;
• Economically disadvantaged persons;
• Persons with limited digital literacy and
• Other persons requiring assistance in accessing digital judicial services.
The service shall be provided without discrimination on any ground.
19. REVIEW OF THE SOP
This SOP shall be reviewed periodically by the competent authority to incorporate:
• Changes in eCourts services;
• Technological developments;
• Changes in applicable rules;
• Feedback from stakeholders;
• Operational experience; and
• Directions issued by the High Court/eCommittee, Supreme Court of India.
12
The competent authority may amend, modify or supplement these Guidelines as and
when considered necessary.
